const jf = game.folders.find(f => f.type === "JournalEntry" && f.name === "Suggestions"); const folder = await Folder.create({ name: "Ardenford — Misfit Spots", type: "JournalEntry", color: "#b0603a" }); const P = (h) => ({ format: 1, content: h }); const intro = `

Four places three misfits wander into, and the stupid thing they do when they get there. Written for a party that is chaotic neutral with a conscience — not heroes, not villains, and capable of being decent when it is cheap enough.

Each spot gives you the same five things: why they end up there, the dumb ideas they will have, what actually goes wrong, who is standing there when it does, and the heart — one moment where being decent costs them something small and real. That last one is the whole point. Skip it and they are just petty criminals; land it and they are your party.

Encounter budget

Three level-2 characters, 2024 DMG: Low 300 XP · Moderate 450 · High 600. Every "if it goes loud" below is costed against that. XP is from the owned Monster Manual: Commoner 10 · Guard / Bandit / Cultist / Warrior Infantry / Noble 25 · Swarm of Rats / Goblin Warrior / Priest Acolyte 50 · Scout / Tough 100 · Spy / Pirate 200 · Bandit Captain / Berserker / Cultist Fanatic 450 · Guard Captain 1,100.

Guards are AC 16. At level 2 that is a real wall — the watch is not a speed bump, it is a reason to run. Guard Captain at 1,100 XP is nearly twice the High budget: he is not an encounter, he is a losing condition.

`; const market = `

Middle Tier · the Western Market square, hours after the grain and produce stalls shut. 168 walls, 14 lights, ambient night sound.

Why misfits end up here

Because it is the one place in Ardenford that is rich and unattended at the same time. The Western Market runs sunrise to sunset; after dark it is canvas, trestles, locked crates and nobody. The watch walks it, but the watch walks through it, on a rhythm you can learn in one night of sitting on a roof.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Crack a crate to see what is in it. Not to steal — to know. This is the most in-character thing a misfit does and it is how every one of these nights starts.
  2. Take the stall, not the goods. Someone will suggest stealing an entire market stall and setting it up somewhere else. Let them. It is very funny and it is very traceable.
  3. Sell something back to its owner in the morning. Genuinely a plan they will be proud of.

What actually goes wrong

The crate is Greystone grain — federal reserve stock, moved at night on purpose, stamped on purpose. Breaking one open is not theft from a merchant, it is interference with the city's siege stores, and Ardenford has a long memory about granaries. Nobody is chasing them for the value. Somebody is chasing them because of what the stamp means.

Who is here

A night porter who is not supposed to be, counting crates against a list that does not match. He is more frightened of being seen than they are. He will bargain instantly.

If it goes loud

The watch turn-out: 4 × Guard (100) + 1 × Scout as the sergeant (100) = 200 XP — under Low, because this is meant to be survivable and humiliating rather than lethal. AC 16 will still make them work for it.
If they stay and fight the second wave: add 4 more Guards (100) → 300 XP, Low. A third wave brings the Guard Captain, and that is the city telling them to leave.

The heart

The porter has a daughter's name on the back of his tally board. If they let him go — or better, let him keep the discrepancy and take the blame for the broken crate themselves — they have made their first real friend in Ardenford, in the Middle Tier, at night, where friends are useful. It costs them the loot and a night in a cell. That is the price, and they should feel it.

`; const baths = `

Upper Tier · members-only, run quietly by the Vintara Consortium. 188 walls, 23 lights, 25 ambient sounds. Warm, dim, and full of people with their clothes off and their guard down.

Why misfits end up here

Because the Council of Consuls rotates its meetings between keeps so no one keep gains significance — which means the actual conversations happen between meetings, somewhere comfortable, with no minutes taken. Everyone in Ardenford knows this. Nobody says it.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Steal the robes and walk in. It works. That is the problem — it works immediately and then they are inside with no plan and no clothes.
  2. Rob the changing room. An unattended room of rich people's belongings. They will not be able to help themselves.
  3. Get in the water and act natural. The single funniest failure state available, because eventually somebody addresses them by a name that is not theirs and expects an answer.

What actually goes wrong

They overhear something true. Not a grand conspiracy — something small, specific and survivable only if you are already important: a consul's aide arranging for a writ to be posted with no name on it. The party now knows a thing that is worth money to exactly one person and worth their lives to another, and they are naked in a bath house on the Upper Tier.

Who is here

The aide, and a bath attendant who has heard this conversation four times and has learned to be extremely interested in the floor. The attendant is the real asset. She notices everything and is paid to notice nothing.

If it goes loud

Discreet removal: 1 × Spy (200) + 2 × Guard (50) = 250 XP, under Low — but the Spy's job is not to kill them, it is to find out who sent them. Capture is the win condition, and a captured misfit is a much better story than a dead one.
If they kill the aide: Vintara answers. Bandit Captain-equivalent as a Consortium officer (450) + 2 × Tough (200) = 650 XP, above High. That is deliberate. They should lose.

The heart

The attendant will be blamed. She was in the room; they were not supposed to be. If the party walks away clean they will hear, three days later and secondhand, that a bath attendant was dismissed and cannot get work on the Upper Tier. Bringing her with them costs them the clean exit and gains them somebody who knows every face in Ardenford's ruling class.

`; const tap = `

Beneath everything · a tavern in the ancient tunnel network, which the Council insists is sealed. 592 walls, 17 lights, 52 ambient sounds — it is the loudest, wettest, most alive map in the set.

Why misfits end up here

Because it should not exist. Every tunnel entrance inside the city is guarded or sealed, the Council is emphatic about it, and there is a bar down there with a full room. Finding it is a status symbol. Being known down there is a career.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Win a drinking contest against a dwarf. Yes. Yes they will.
  2. Run a tab. Nobody down here uses coin for everything, and the alternative currency is favours. They will find this out after the third round.
  3. Ask loudly how everyone gets in and out. The one question that gets a room to stop talking.

What actually goes wrong

Nothing, at first — and that is the trap. They are welcomed, fed, and on the way out somebody hands them a sealed package and a name, in a tone that makes it clear this is the tab being settled, not a request. Refusing is allowed. Refusing means they were down here, they saw it, and they owe nothing — which makes them a loose end rather than an asset.

Who is here

Working dwarves who move goods under the city because the surface routes are taxed and watched. They are not villains and should not read as villains: this is an economy, not a cult. Khargrom-dur (Ardenford — Townsfolk) fits perfectly as the one who vouches for them — a valley guide is exactly the sort who knows the ways under as well as the ways east.

If it goes loud

The room turns: 6 × Bandit as off-shift smugglers (150) + 2 × Tough (200) = 350 XP, just over Low — in a flooded, pillared, 592-wall space where line of sight is terrible and everyone but the party knows the floor plan.
Do not let them win by killing. The tunnels are a place they need to be able to come back to. Give the room a reason to break it up.

The heart

One of the smugglers is moving medicine, not contraband — Willowglass stock, cheaper under the city than over it, going to Gray District families who cannot pay Upper Tier prices. If the party burns the tunnel to the watch for a reward, that supply stops. Nobody will ever tell them that happened. That is the version of consequence that works on a party with hearts: not punishment, just a thing quietly getting worse somewhere they cannot see.

`; const library = `

Upper Tier, Ridge District · built into and around an intact ancient structure. 456 walls, 13 ambient sounds, no placed lighting — see the note below.

Why misfits end up here

Because the Ruins Reclamation Act made ruin-delving legal and profitable, and the Concordance holds the maps and the old expedition reports. Every treasure hunter in Ardenford comes through here. The party will come here for a map and leave with a problem.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Just take the book. The entire plan. There is no second step.
  2. Tear the page out so the book stays on the shelf and nobody notices. Somehow worse.
  3. Get one of them to distract the Magister. This will involve a false accent and it will not survive contact.

What actually goes wrong

They are not caught by the Magister. They are caught by Elarion Faenwynd, the elf archivist, who does not raise an alarm — he asks what they are looking for. And he can read what they cannot. Whatever they wanted is genuinely in his hands now, and he has decided to be curious about them instead of turning them in. They have accidentally acquired a patron, and they will not notice for several sessions.

Who is here

Magister Ellyn Merrick — stern, protective, believes knowledge should be shared provided you handle it with respect. She is not an obstacle to beat; she is an obstacle to impress, and she can be impressed.
Elarion Faenwynd — archivist and translator, guest scholar from Araethilion. Both are already built in Ardenford — Townsfolk.
Pell Orvaine at The Still Page, one lane over, knows every Concordance staffer's tea order and is a soft way in for a party that thinks to try being nice.

If it goes loud

It should not. The Concordance is the spot in this set that punishes violence with irrelevance — fight here and the doors close to them permanently, which costs more than any fight. If you must: 2 × Priest Acolyte (100) + 4 × Guard (100) = 200 XP, and the real consequence is being barred, not beaten.

The heart

Elarion is far from home and nobody in this city can pronounce his name. If a player asks how to say it properly — eh-LAR-ee-on FAYN-wind — and gets it right, he will help them with things he is not supposed to help them with, for years. It costs nothing but attention. Misfits who are bad at everything except noticing people are the best kind.

⚠ Map note

This scene ships with zero lights. If you run it with token vision on, the party is in the dark in a library. Either set the scene's global illumination on, or lean into it and run it after closing.

`; const je = await JournalEntry.create({ name: "Ardenford — Misfit Spots", folder: folder.id, pages: [ { name: "How to run these", type: "text", text: P(intro) }, { name: "1 · Western Market, after dark", type: "text", text: P(market) }, { name: "2 · The Vintara Baths", type: "text", text: P(baths) }, { name: "3 · The Drowned Tap", type: "text", text: P(tap) }, { name: "4 · The Concordance Library", type: "text", text: P(library) }, ], }); return { journal: je.name, folder: folder.name, pages: je.pages.map(p => p.name) };

On the board — 7

The situation: a buy is happening at the fountain at the worst possible hour, and the one honest witness is forty feet away with his own reason to say nothing.

  • Sella Redcott (green — talkable) · at the fountain. Buying something off a seller who has already left. She is not dangerous herself; the two at the braziers are hers and she will spend them without blinking. Lever: she pays under value and knows it. A party that has something to sell has an instant in.
  • Redcott's Man ×2 (grey — muscle) · under the two lit braziers, west and east. Deliberately placed on the plaza's two lit approaches, so the party is already between them before anyone speaks. Not a wall — a pair of eyes that will follow.
  • Wick Harlow (green) · south-west crate stack. Counting federal Greystone crates against a tally that does not match, because he has been skimming one sack in forty for eleven months. His daughter's name is inked on the back of the board. Lever: he will bargain instantly, and he will not fight.
  • Three nobodies (ringless) · a sweeper closing a west stall, a young woman cutting through the south stalls, an old man on the stoop of the lit house. They are there to make it a place rather than a set, and to make "nobody saw us" a lie.

To pick a fight: walk between the braziers. To be in the way: the sweeper is closing the exact stall they want. As a lever: Harlow's tally board — it is evidence against a consul's supplier and against Harlow, and he knows it.

`; const baths = `

On the board — 7

The situation: the aide thinks the baths are safe because they always have been. Everyone else in the building is either naked, working, or paid to stand still.

  • Aldric Dunwick (green) · the middle private soaking room, east side. Mid-conversation about a writ posted with no name on it. Isolated by design — the party can reach him, but only past the minder.
  • Vintara Minder ×2 (grey) · the corridor outside the private rooms, and the head of the entrance stair. One covers the prize, one covers the way they came in. Neither is looking at the canal dock in the south-west — that is the way in the map is quietly offering.
  • Nessa Brightmoor (green) · the attendant's desk, west. Has heard this conversation four times. Knows every face in Ardenford's ruling class by the state of their feet. Lever: the single best-informed person in the building and the only one nobody is watching.
  • Three nobodies · two in the main pool, one in the banquet room. Unarmed, unclothed, and extremely willing to scream.

To pick a fight: the corridor minder, in a tiled room, with no armour on anyone. To be in the way: the bathers between the pool and the private rooms. As a lever: Nessa — and remember she is the one dismissed for it if strangers are found, which is the page's heart.

`; const tap = `

On the board — 8

The situation: nothing is wrong. The room is warm, the welcome is real, and the tab is running whether they asked for one or not.

  • Brogmar-dur (green) · behind the counter. Keeps the place. Runs no coin tab — the currency is favours and he decides what one is worth. Lever: genuinely hospitable, which is exactly how the debt gets made.
  • Khargrom-dur (green) · the round table. Already a townsfolk actor. He is the one who vouches for them, which is why the room relaxes — and why they owe him before they owe anyone else.
  • Tunnel Runner ×2 (grey) · shifting barrels on the walkway below the tap, and on the east walkway. Working, not watching. One of them is moving Willowglass medicine, not contraband — see the heart, above.
  • Tap Lookout (grey) · head of the stair down. The only one whose job is the party. Placed so leaving is a decision, not a default.
  • Three nobodies · a drinker at the second table, someone at the kitchen hearth, a boy running messages on the lower walkway. The boy is the fastest way for news of the party to reach anywhere in the undercity.

To pick a fight: ask loudly how everyone gets in and out. To be in the way: the Lookout on the stair. As a lever: the tab — and the boy, who can carry a message anywhere down here for the price of being nice to him once.

`; const library = `

On the board — 6

The situation: quiet, sparse, and the most dangerous room in the set — because losing here costs them access, not hit points.

  • Magister Ellyn Merrick (green) · the long reading hall. Stern, protective, believes knowledge should be shared provided you handle it with respect. Not an obstacle to beat — an obstacle to impress, and she can be impressed.
  • Elarion Faenwynd (green) · the north shelves, cataloguing. Positioned exactly where a thief would reach for a book. He is the one who catches them, and he does not raise the alarm — he asks what they are looking for.
  • Corr Ashgate (grey) · the east apse, watching. A ruin-delver with a forged Reclamation writ, after the same report. Happy to let the party take the risk and then take the map off them outside. The only one here who will start something — and he will do it in the street, not in the building.
  • Ardenford Watch (grey) · the south stair. One guard, AC 16, CR 1/8. He is not a fight, he is a witness, and that is worse.
  • Two nobodies · an apprentice copying at the south bench, someone crossing the lower chamber.

To pick a fight: don't — take it outside with Ashgate, who wants exactly that. To be in the way: the apprentice is at the desk they need. As a lever: Elarion, if a player bothers to learn to say his name.

${line}

Type: ${type}

Was: ${was}
